source: docs/revamp/04-ARCHITECTURE.md §8.2 (the lab performance targets) and §8.4 ("Lighthouse budgets"), docs/revamp/05-MIGRATION.md §3 item C11, RC-06 and RC-18. Written by WO-29.
$comment: WHAT THIS FILE IS. The §8.2 table, encoded once per audited state and once per form factor,
as Lighthouse CI assertions. Nothing here is a preference: every ceiling below is the number
in 04-ARCHITECTURE.md §8.2, and 04 §8.4's ratchet rule governs it exactly as it governs
web/budgets.json -- a ceiling may only move in a PR that edits this file in the same commit
and says why in the PR body. web/tests/lighthouserc.test.ts re-states §8.2 independently and
fails on any drift, so the two cannot quietly diverge.
THREE PROFILES, BECAUSE LIGHTHOUSE HAS ONE FORM FACTOR PER RUN. `collect.settings` is global
to an `lhci autorun` invocation, so the same URL cannot be audited at two form factors in one
run. `ci` below IS the mobile-412 profile -- a bare `npx lhci autorun` from web/ runs it and
asserts the mobile half of §8.2 -- and `profiles` carries the other two as complete,
literal, `ci`-shaped configs. Nothing is generated or merged: `scripts/lhci-run.mjs` writes
each one to disk verbatim and hands it to `lhci autorun --config`. The duplication is
deliberate and is gated by the test rather than removed by a merge step, because a merge step
is the thing that makes a config file stop meaning what it reads as.
THE FOUR STATES are the four with retained Gate 1 baseline JSON and Gate 3 rerun JSON
(docs/revamp/evidence/gate-3/lighthouse-diff.md §3): landing, empty conversation, populated
report, plan review. `mobile-320` adds 04 §8.3's narrow-strip width for the two states the
Gate 3 pack audited there. The URLs are the seeded stack's `baseline-*` fixtures, written by
web/e2e/fixtures/seed.sh directly into Postgres and Redis -- POST /research is never called,
so no model provider is contacted by anything in this file.
BASE URL. The host below is `web/e2e/support/stack.sh`'s default, which is what CI uses.
`scripts/lhci-run.mjs` substitutes $LHCI_BASE_URL when it is set, for a stack on another port.
Every `matchingUrlPattern` is host-agnostic (`^https?://[^/]+/...`) so the assertions bind to
the route, not to the port that happened to be free.
AGGREGATION, STATED RATHER THAN DEFAULTED. LHCI's default `aggregationMethod` is
"optimistic" -- the friendliest of the three runs. That is not a gate, so every assertion
below sets the method explicitly:
* median   for the four throttled, noisy measurements (LCP, TBT, CLS, Performance). These
are simulated-throttling figures on shared CI hardware; PR #111 measured the same
URL at LCP 1.29 s and 2.49 s in consecutive samples, so a worst-of-three gate
would report the runner's mood, not the application's.
* pessimistic for Accessibility, Best Practices and bf-cache. These are deterministic audits
with no throttling term, so "the worst run must also be 100" costs nothing and
is what §8.2's "100, not approximated" actually means. A `minScore` of 1 on a
Lighthouse category is exact: category scores are capped at 1.
`includePassedAssertions` IS ON, IN ALL THREE PROFILES. LHCI writes only FAILED assertions to
`.lighthouseci/assertion-results.json` by default, so a green run leaves behind an empty
array -- indistinguishable from a run that asserted nothing at all, which is the exact claim
this file has to be able to prove. With the flag on, the artifact carries one row per
evaluated assertion (70 of them), and the exit code is unchanged: `lhci assert` fails on
`!passed && level === "error"` either way.
CLS AND RC-06. The gate is ≤ 0.02 (04 §8.2). The design intent is 0.000 (03-DESIGN-BRIEF.md
§3.5, §5.6, design/tokens.json "cls-budget"). RC-06 resolves the two as answers to different
questions and requires a written justification for any state that lands above 0.000. Both the
measured values and those justifications are in
docs/revamp/evidence/gate-4/lhci/README.md §4 -- not here, because a measurement belongs in
an evidence pack with the run that produced it.
BF-CACHE AND RC-18, INCLUDING THE ONE DOCUMENTED DEVIATION. RC-18 requires the `bf-cache`
audit to pass on `/c/[id]`. It is asserted at `error` on every MOBILE cell -- all four states
at 412 px and both states at 320 px -- because that is where it measurably passes.
It is asserted at `warn` on every DESKTOP cell, and that is a deviation with a measured cause
rather than a threshold that was found inconvenient.
The cause, in two parts. (1) Since WO-30 (#109) the root layout reads the per-request CSP
nonce from `headers()`, which opts EVERY document route into dynamic rendering, and Next
serves a dynamic document with
`Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. A nonce-based CSP
and a bfcache-eligible cacheable document are mutually exclusive; web/middleware.ts says so
in its own header. Lighthouse reports exactly that -- `MainResourceHasCacheControlNoStore`
plus `JsNetworkRequestReceivedCacheControlNoStoreResource`, both classified
"Not actionable". (2) Chrome nevertheless ADMITS the same document to bfcache under mobile
emulation and refuses it under desktop emulation, on all four states, reproducibly, on both
Lighthouse 13.4.1 (the Gate 3 pack) and the 12.6.1 that @lhci/cli pins. So the deviation is
shaped by form factor, not by route: `/` passes on mobile and `/c/[id]` fails on desktop.
The lhci README §5 records the isolation runs, including the one that rules the user agent
out and the reason `formFactor` and `screenEmulation.mobile` cannot be varied independently.
`warn` rather than `off` on the desktop cells, on purpose: the audit still runs and still
prints on every nightly, so the day the constraint lifts we see it instead of having deleted
the question.

profiles.label: Desktop, 1350 x 940
$comment: Lighthouse's own `--preset=desktop`, written out rather than referenced: @lhci/cli has no
`preset` option, so `collect.settings` has to carry what the preset would have set.
The four values are core/config/desktop-config.js + core/config/constants.js from the
pinned Lighthouse (`desktopDense4G`, `screenEmulationMetrics.desktop`,
`userAgents.desktop`), and tests/lighthouserc.test.ts pins them so a Lighthouse bump that
changes the preset cannot silently change what 'desktop' means here.
The desktop budgets are the tighter half of §8.2: LCP ≤ 1.20 s, TBT ≤ 50 ms, Perf ≥ 98.

profiles.label: Mobile, 320 x 568 (04 §8.3 narrow strip)
$comment: 04 §8.3 audits the narrow-strip repair at 320 px and the Gate 3 pack ran two states there
(`home-320.gate3.json`, `conversation-populated-320.gate3.json`). Same mobile budgets as
the 412 profile -- §8.2 has one mobile column, not one per width -- and the same
throttling; only the viewport differs, which is the point of the width.
Two states rather than four, matching the Gate 3 pack exactly, so the nightly's 320 px row
is comparable to a retained measurement instead of being a new claim with no before.
